study type: retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
outcome: incidence of non-cephalic presentation at 36-week scan
uptake and success of external cephalic version (ECV)
incidence of spontaneous rotation from non-cephalic to cephalic presentation
cohort: The study included 107,875 women with a singleton pregnancy who had a routine ultrasound scan at 35 + 0 to 36 + 6 weeks' gestation.
finding: At the 36-week scan, 5.8% of singleton pregnancies presented non-cephalic, and a combination of successful ECV (44.1% success rate) and spontaneous rotation (37.7% among those without successful ECV) ultimately led to 43.8% of these fetuses being cephalic at birth, though the predictive performance of maternal and pregnancy characteristics for these events was poor.
mod_finding: Among pregnancies with non-cephalic presentation at 36 weeks, 43.8% had cephalic presentation at birth, with 74.8% of these attributed to spontaneous rotation and 25.2% to successful external cephalic version.
gest_age: 35 + 0 to 36 + 6 weeks' gestation (at time of scan)
